text:
anna: Heads-up — after merging PR #3421 the canary is doing a big compile backfill. p95 latency up ~30% for short-seq traffic. canary is paused.

anna: quick top-level evidence: kernel compile queue depth jumped and we're seeing lots of small-kernel picks that bypass the vectorized path. snippet from runtime logs:```
[2026-03-18T14:06:12Z] kernel_autopick: chosen_kernel=nonvec_v1 score=-2.1 fallback=vec_v2 score=-2.0
[2026-03-18T14:06:12Z] compile_queue.enqueue(model=redwood-y-7b, kernel=nonvec_v1)
[2026-03-18T14:06:13Z] kvcache.invalidate_prefix(prefix="/sessions/", count=240)
```

mike: do we have a flame or p-stack?

anna: flame: https://perf.internal/redwood/trace/2245006789 (short sequences filter applied). main hotspot looks like compile-lock wait and a bunch of small JIT kernels being used.

dmitri: looking at infra metrics — kvcache invalidations spiked at the same time the compile backlog started. suggests something is regressing the cache-keying or we are evicting too aggressively. evictions/s = +8x.

ramon: my hunch: PR #3421 changed the compile-selector scoring weights (the tie-breaker lambda). maybe it made the selector favor lower-memory kernels which are slower per-token.

sara: I ran a local repro against the canary image with the short-seq harness:```bash
# reproduce harness
python tests/harness.py --model redwood-y-7b --seq 32 --qps 60 --duration 60
# profiler shows autopick selecting nonvec for many batches
```
outputs: avg_token_latency_nonvec=5.6ms avg_token_latency_vec=3.2ms

infra-bot: CI perf job perf/shortseq/stability failed on commit abc1234 (PR #3421). Details: https://ci.internal/job/perf/2245006700

jeff: if CI already caught it, can we revert the PR to unblock release and then re-land with tests?

anna: canary is already held, but we should bisect to confirm the exact commit. if it's just the lambda tweak, revert is low-risk.

mike: starting bisect now. I'll try a narrow range: commits abc1200..abc1300. will report back in ~10m.

mike: bisect result: culprit is abc1234 — the change to selector::score_tiebreaker (see diff: https://git.internal/r/changes/abc1234).

dmitri: that matches the kvcache spike — the new tiebreaker picks kernels that avoid KV-cache-friendly codepaths, which increases cache churn.

ramon: proposed quick revert patch (manual):```diff
- // prefer smaller memory footprint as tie-breaker
- score += -0.5 * mem_estimate;
+ // revert to preferring vectorized path on tie
+ // keep memory consideration but weaker
+ score += -0.1 * mem_estimate;
```

sara: can we instead add a canary-only flag: selectors.retain_vectorized_on_tie=true so we don't flip global behavior until we validate?

jeff: yes do that first. low-risk config flip on canary, then revert PR if needed.

anna: I pushed a canary config change to keep vectorized preference and redeployed canary. Monitoring closely.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused for redwood-y-7b (reason: manual hold).

mike: post-change metrics look better: compile_queue.depth down 80%, p95 back to baseline. we'll keep the config flag until a proper unit/integration test is added.

dmitri: follow-ups: add regression test that simulates short-seq traffic with randomized tie conditions; add a metric alert for kernel-selection-entropy and kvcache-eviction-rate.

anna: assigning follow-ups: mike -> write bisect notes and patch; sara -> add canary-only selector flag and tests; dmitri -> kvcache alert. I'll draft the rollback note for the release ticket.

jeff: thanks everyone. tagging infra for any rollback assistance: @infra-oncall

anna: TL;DR: PR #3421 changed selector tiebreaker, caused wrong kernel picks and kvcache churn. canary paused, config flip applied, perf recovered. will follow up with tests and proper fix. :white_check_mark:
